name: Hashabnah
overview: Hashabnah is a male biblical figure identified as a non-Levite leader mentioned in Nehemiah 10:25. His role is noted within the context of a sealed document listing leaders and signatories. Although his tribal affiliation is not specified, his inclusion among the leaders highlights his recognized position during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Hashabnah likely means "Yahweh has considered me," reflecting a theologically significant meaning rooted in the divine name. This proper name, as recorded in Nehemiah 10:25, does not indicate that it was given directly by God but carries a sense of divine attention or favor.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Hashabnah is a descendant of Jacob, establishing his connection to the patriarchal lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hashabnah's significance lies in his role as a non-Levite leader who was among those who sealed the covenant documented in Nehemiah 10. His inclusion demonstrates the involvement of various leaders in reaffirming the community's commitment to God's law after the exile. This highlights the unity and dedication of Israel's leaders, including those outside the Levitical priesthood, in the restoration efforts.
